description: The vertex rule's perspective divide is not measured: every terrain projection is orthographic (clip w = 1 on all 973,749 corpus vertices), so window_of_ divides by w in float (ndc = clip * f32(1 / w)) only as a guess for w != 1; no port path draws with w != 1.
needed: a feedback probe with glFrustum / a perspective matrix

description: The float32 rotation matrix is measured for the terrain's axis-aligned rotations (every element formula gives the same floats there) and for one general axis (37 degrees about (0.3, 0.7, 0.5): the diagonal must be x^2 + (1 - x^2) c, rows 0 and 1 off-diagonal (1 - c) x y -+ s z fit); row 2's off-diagonal terms, the cos / sin source (double cos of the double radians rounded to float, or float radians) and the axis normalisation (divide vs multiply by the inverse) are not separated by any probe (all variants equal on the tested angles).
needed: a probe sweeping general axes and angles with points near ties

description: The real GL's triangle feedback gives texture coordinates for clipped vertices of blocks drawn with texture 0 bound (incomplete, untextured) that are not the interpolated ones (the same (0.453, 0.547) / (1.0, 0.203) recur on unrelated triangles of c7/fuzz1_z0: 36 of 3,933 triangles); positions are exact. No pixel reads them (the fragment is the lit colour), so GlRaster interpolates them like any other; colour interpolation of clipped vertices (float lerp from the inside vertex) is assumed the texcoords' rule, not measured on its own.
needed: triangle feedback of a textured probe and an untextured one crossing the edge

description: GlRaster still lights vertices in double: the real GL's feedback colour differs by up to 1.4e-7 (c7/fuzz1_z0: 2,981 of 31,650 channel values float-equal to the double result cast; sandbox 27,211 of 27,459), i.e. at most 4e-5 of an 8-bit level after the texel product; tune 12 (every lighting intermediate float32) changes no pixel of the seven c7 passes measured. The pixels within 1e-4 of a 5-bit boundary among the remaining one-level ones are in reach of this difference.
needed: fit the float lighting order against the feedback colours (21_litfit.py has the data path)

description: The rest of U-1392 after the vertex and clip rules (one-level px of the 271 stream passes 18,234 -> 2,296) is the attribute interpolation: the generic GL steps attributes incrementally in fixed point. Measured (21_ramp.py dense, 21_interpfit.py edgewalk): rows walk from the vertex of largest y; a row start = the previous row start + trunc(31 * 2^16 * (-dv/dy * rows + dv/dx * dx)) / (31 * 2^16) (colour in the 5-bit range, 16.16 fixed, truncated), span pixels + trunc(31 * 2^16 * dv/dx) / (31 * 2^16), the first row exact: a slow ramp probe 0 of 477,802 px wrong (exact plane 705), random Gouraud quads 480 -> 90 (all 90 in triangles with a horizontal top edge, deep in their walk; floor / rounding, separate x / y steps, float32 gradients and 2^-8..2^-30 edge DDAs do not remove them). Texture coordinates are assumed to step the same way (the bilinear probe residue has the same size), not measured. S3.21b put it in GlRaster's general loop as opt-in `#tune 30` (default off): exact on the untextured ramp, but under GL_MODULATE every stepped variant (colour quanta 31 / 255 / 1 x 2^16, texture coordinates at 2^-8..2^-16 texel) is worse than the plane on the textured probes, and on the c7 terrain passes untextured-only stepping changes nothing (173 / 22): the terrain residue is the textured interpolation, not measured.
needed: the 90 px of the Gouraud probe (row start after an x-schedule change, first-row start), a slow-ramp probe of a texture coordinate and of the colour over a constant texture (21_ramp.py's method), then the fast loop
